outcome.answer: Yes. The closest matches are [1], [2], [3], and [5]: they all address updating item identifiers or token mappings in generative retrieval/recommendation as item behavior changes. [1] specifically argues to keep old SIDs fixed, insert new items, and warm-start training so the model preserves learned topology, while [2] proposes a lightweight SID alignment update to refresh interaction-informed SIDs without a full rebuild. [3] adds an exposure-aware dynamic update mechanism for a large semantic codebook, and [5] uses drift-aware continual tokenization with drift detection and hierarchical code reassignment to limit disruptive changes.
